newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivorian cocoa bean exports rise in September.
newsitem.headline: Ivorian cocoa bean exports rise in September.

text.p: Ivory Coast's cocoa bean exports rose slightly to 6,081 tonnes in September from a thin 4,400 tonnes in August, official data show.

Exporters had expected low volumes as farmers held on to stocks ahead of the new 1996/97 cocoa marketing season which opened late on October 24. The season usually opens in early October, making temporary stocking worthwhile for farmers if higher prices are expected.
Exports in September last year amounted to 10,020 tonnes.
Exports to Tallin in Estonia of 3,303 tonnes exceeded exports to the usual first destinations of Amsterdam, with 1,116 tonnes in September, and the United States, with no shipments.

Cumulative exports for the first 12 months of the 1995/96 (Oct-Sept) season were 1,064,548 tonnes against 760,054 tonnes in the same period of the 1994/95 season. Export figures for October 1-24 were not immediately available and will slightly raise the final (Oct-Sep) season export totals.
Ivory Coast's 1996/97 crop is forecast down this year with exporters expecting between 850,000 to 900,000 tonnes against a record 1.2 million tonnes in 1995/96.
Ivory Coast's commodities minister Guy-Alain Gauze recently forecast 1996/97 production in a 900,000-950,000 tonnes range.
